question.text: Circular trading (wash trades) in the derivatives market involves:

answer.text: Executing trades between connected parties with no genuine change in beneficial ownership, to create artificial volume or price
Trading in multiple derivative products simultaneously
Rolling over positions from one expiry to another
Trading through multiple brokers for better execution

explanation.text: The Logic: As a matter of general market-manipulation principles, circular or wash trades involve buy and sell orders executed between the same beneficial owner or among connected parties with no genuine change in beneficial ownership. The purpose is to manufacture artificial volume or price movement, misleading other participants into believing there is real demand or supply in the security. This is recognised as a form of fraudulent and unfair trade practice in Indian securities regulation. The Trap: Rolling over positions from one expiry to another is a legitimate derivatives activity, not manipulation. Trading in multiple derivatives products or through multiple brokers for execution reasons is also legal. Only trades lacking a genuine economic transfer of ownership amount to circular/wash trading. Note: The specific PFUTP-style definition of circular/wash trading (no genuine change in beneficial ownership, artificial volume) is not spelled out in the cited NISM Series VIII Equity Derivatives workbook pages; the explanation above reflects general securities-regulation knowledge rather than a workbook citation.
